content.text:
The drawing shows indigo carmine (indigotine disodium sulfonate) in a tautomeric form. Reading it region by region:

- **Left ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. The five-membered ring has a C=O carbon, then a carbon double-bonded to N (C=N), and the N is bonded to the aromatic carbon. A sulfonate (S(=O)(=O)[O-]) sits on the benzene ring.
- **Right ring system:** a benzene ring fused to a five-membered ring. This ring has a C-OH carbon double-bonded to the carbon that is joined to the left unit, and an NH bonded to the aromatic carbon. It carries a second sulfonate on the benzene ring.
- **Link and counterions:** a single bond joins the left C=N carbon to the right C2 carbon. Two Na+ ions are shown.

Writing the left unit: O=C1C(=Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc12)...

The left C=O carbon is attached to the aromatic carbon at the top, which is adjacent to the CH that bears the sulfonate neighbour. The sulfonate-bearing carbon is attached to the top-left CH, which connects to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to C=O. So the sulfonate is para to N's ring-fusion carbon, as in the SMILES above: c2 (attached to N), c, c, c(S), c, c12.

Right unit: C2 (=C(O)c3cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc3N2). The C-OH carbon is attached to the ring-fusion carbon at the top, then the CH, then the carbon bearing S, then two CH, then the ring-fusion carbon bonded to NH.

Full SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].O=C1C(=Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc12)C1=C(O)c2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc2N1

SMILES: [Na+].[Na+].O=C1C(=Nc2ccc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])cc12)C1=C(O)c2cc(S(=O)(=O)[O-])ccc2N1
